I work with this tech heavily. And while you’re right. It’s also not doing a great job of a lot of the things. You suggest. 

At work we’ve handed Claude and Gemini the same document - containing staff details. In both cases it’s output invented members of staff that were never employed. In some cases they were members of well known bands. 

On the code front - it might be finding bugs. But it’s also adding new ones and generating code that is overly complex, more overwrought than it needs to be and as such is much more brittle and prone to failure when things go wrong. 

Language translation - this is hilarious because while it can. It doesn’t mean it can do it accurately. And unlike the example of the documents where it’s added none staff to it. Unless you’re multi lingual you have little immediate way to spot errors. 

It’s a stochastic parrot, it presents a mathematically predicted “best” answer based on the data that we’ve e fed it during training - it can and often does get things wrong because of poor weighting of information in its training data. 

It will also, often present entirely different data to different people with the same core data set and prompt. Depending on its ongoing context with that user. 

Can it be useful? Sure. But that usefulness needs to be factored against the cost of it being wrong and the cost of actually verifying its output - and that latter point is starting to swing more to just doing the work yourself or hiring someone to were you can’t.

@pilgrimoftheworldalso worth noting that the uses you gave aren’t generative AI, they were all possible with earlier models of machine learning. The massive hyper-scaling going on now is to pursue generative AI which is much harder to justify given the unbelievable costs

I work with this tech heavily. And while you’re right. It’s also not doing a great job of a lot of the things. You suggest. 

At work we’ve handed Claude and Gemini the same document - containing staff details. In both cases it’s output invented members of staff that were never employed. In some cases they were members of well known bands. 

On the code front - it might be finding bugs. But it’s also adding new ones and generating code that is overly complex, more overwrought than it needs to be and as such is much more brittle and prone to failure when things go wrong. 

Language translation - this is hilarious because while it can. It doesn’t mean it can do it accurately. And unlike the example of the documents where it’s added none staff to it. Unless you’re multi lingual you have little immediate way to spot errors. 

It’s a stochastic parrot, it presents a mathematically predicted “best” answer based on the data that we’ve e fed it during training - it can and often does get things wrong because of poor weighting of information in its training data. 

It will also, often present entirely different data to different people with the same core data set and prompt. Depending on its ongoing context with that user. 

Can it be useful? Sure. But that usefulness needs to be factored against the cost of it being wrong and the cost of actually verifying its output - and that latter point is starting to swing more to just doing the work yourself or hiring someone to were you can’t.
